1.why: Text uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and short line lengths, though letter spacing appears default rather than explicitly widened.

2.why: All copy is short sentence-case text with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs on any screen.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single column with full-width controls and ample whitespace, reading well at mobile width.

4.why: Instructions are one-line plain-language sentences such as 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.'

5.why: Every input shows an example of expected input via placeholders ('name@example.com', 'Example: 123456').

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a couple of short sentences to proceed.

7.why: The verification code had to be typed by hand and no copy-to-clipboard control appears on any screen, while the screens holding long secrets (authenticator secret, recovery codes) were never shown.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears anywhere; the flow never advanced past step 2 of 4.

9.why: Screenshots cannot confirm autocomplete support; the standard email/password fields would work with password managers by default, but the OTP field shows no visible autofill affordance.

10.why: The step banner ('Step 2 of 4 - Check identity') is clear, but after a code is sent the screen shows two filled primary buttons (Send code and Check code), so the primary action no longer stands out.

11.why: From the code-sent screen onward the user faces three simultaneous actions (Send code, Check code, Send a new code), two of them styled as primary.

12.why: Status banners plainly state what happened and what comes next, e.g. 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

13.why: The user can re-check the code or use 'Send a new code' without any visible penalty, and the code is entered as visible plain text, though no explicit reveal/hide toggle exists.

14.why: The error 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.' states the problem and the fix without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown or time limit is visible anywhere, and wording like 'Enter it when you are ready' explicitly removes time pressure.
